To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the repetitive frequency laser resistances of optical coatings were characterized experimentally, and the stable laser fluence of a damage probability curve peak could be employed to describe the repetitive frequency laser damage threshold.

the laser fluence of a slight damage pattern is stable as the pulse sequence S changes, and the stable laser fluence can be employed to characterize optical coatings’ repetitive frequency laser resistance.

the stable laser fluence of the peak of the damage probability curve can be used as a parameter to characterize the repetitive laser resistance of optical coating, which is different from ISO 11254-3 and has the advantage in practical applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the damage threshold of optics, the method to characterize the laser resistance, and its practical application.
the characterization of repetitive frequency damage resistance of optical coatings.
the development of an experimental technique to characterize repetitive frequency (S) laser resistance of optics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method for characterization of repetitive-frequency laser resistance of optical coating is based on the slight damage pattern, and the laser resistance can be characterized by the laser fluence of the peak in the damage probability curves.
this method is an effective way for characterization of repetitive laser resistance of optical coating, and it can be used in laser damage testing.
the method proposed in this paper is more accurate and practical than the method proposed by ISO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the damage threshold of optical coatings is the laser fluence that can make 50% of the total number of the slight damage patterns.
the damage pattern divided into the slight damage and severe one can be employed to characterize laser resistance of optics.
the slight damage pattern can be used to characterize the repetitive laser damage of optical coatings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser damage threshold is a functional threshold that is dependent upon the laser fluence, the number of pulses, and the repetition frequency of the laser pulse.
, for the characterization of repetitive frequency damage threshold, the damage pattern should be divided into slight damage pattern and severe damage pattern.
, for the same optical coating, the damage probability curve obtained from the slight damage pattern has a peak, and the laser energy at this peak is the functional damage threshold.
